references.text: Jesus proclaims that all who are in the graves shall hear his voice and come out, a direct parallel to the claim that the dead brother will rise.
Jesus confirms that it is the Father's will that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him shall have eternal life and be raised on the last day, which supports the promise of resurrection.
Jesus emphasizes that no one can come to him unless the Father draws them, and that he himself will raise them up on the last day, a repetition of the theme of divine resurrection.
Jesus promises that whoever eats his flesh and drinks his blood has eternal life, and that he will raise him up on the last day, directly linked to the promise of resurrection.
Jesus expresses the Father's will that he should not lose anything of what he has been given, but raise it up on the last day, a central motif supporting the claim that the dead will rise.
